Question: Describe your SDKs (Python minimum; TypeScript desirable) with programmatic access to all platform capabilities. Which agent frameworks are supported (LangChain, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, ADK, MAF)?
Response: Two complementary pro-code SDKs. (1) Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 — Python and .NET — authoring workflow graphs of typed executors (plain-function, agent, validator) with Pregel BSP execution, conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in, checkpointing and native pause/resume. GA Oct 2025. Supports sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat and Magentic-One orchestration patterns. Integrates with Azure Durable Functions via the productised MAF Durable Task extension ("Durable Agent Orchestration" pattern, Feb 2026). (2) GHCP SDK — Python and TypeScript — the agent executor runtime: session creation, skill loading, MCP tool integration, session hooks (`onPreToolUse`/`onPostToolUse`), OTEL instrumentation, model selection from the Foundry catalog. MIT licensed. Inside a MAF agent executor node, you invoke a GHCP SDK session. Developer experience: define agent behaviour via SKILL.md files (declarative capabilities), implement validators as plain functions, wire the graph in MAF, deploy via Azure Functions + Foundry Hosted Agents. Local dev + CLI tooling. Framework interoperability: Semantic Kernel, LangChain and other frameworks can participate via MCP.
Key Technologies: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 (Python/.NET), MAF Durable Task extension, GHCP SDK (Python + TypeScript), Foundry model catalog, MCP protocol, Azure API Center
POC Demo: POC1: Walk through authoring a MAF workflow graph in Python (plain-function + agent + validator executors), building a custom MCP server, defining a skill, configuring GHCP SDK hooks, and deploying via the MAF Durable Task extension on Azure Functions + Foundry Hosted Agents.

Question: Describe your visual workflow builder for defining agent orchestrations, tool bindings, and HITL touchpoints. Is it suitable for citizen developers?
Response: Low-code surfaces. (1) PRIMARY — Microsoft Copilot Studio: Microsoft's flagship low-code agent builder. Visual drag-and-drop designer for conversational and workflow agents — conditional branching, tool bindings (Power Platform connectors + MCP), HITL touchpoints, knowledge grounding. Suitable for citizen developers and domain experts. Copilot Studio agents export as declarative YAML / JSON within Power Platform solutions, Git-committable via Power Platform ALM, versioned through environments (Dev → Test → Prod), and deployed through the same governance pipeline as pro-code agents. Copilot Studio agents register in Agent 365 with first-class Entra Agent ID, are governed by APIM, Purview, and Defender, and appear alongside GHCP SDK agents in the Control Plane. This meets §6.5 'Low-code artefacts must serialise to the same code/config format as pro-code artefacts' via declarative serialisation + Git-committable artefacts + shared governance pathway. (2) Azure Logic Apps for low-code MCP TOOLS: citizen developers chain prebuilt connectors (1,400+ to SharePoint, Outlook, Dataverse, SAP, ServiceNow) and the Logic App is exposed as an MCP tool via APIM's REST→MCP gateway — no-code path for adding tools to the agent ecosystem without writing Python. Governed identically to hand-written MCP servers (auth, rate limits, content safety, audit). (3) Custom Control Plane UI for operational configuration — autonomy threshold dials, tool catalogue view, governance rule editor, skill library (browse, fork, customise pro-code templates backed by Azure API Center); all changes written back to Git through APIOps. This is for operational tuning by process owners, not agent construction. (4) Note on .NET parity: MAF ships with full .NET parity — teams preferring C# build against MAF .NET with the same skills, MCPs, and governance; artefacts serialise identically. For complex autonomous multi-step workflows that need deterministic graph primitives (validator chains, crystallisation pipelines), pro-code (GHCP SDK + MAF) is the recommended path; Copilot Studio excels at the breadth of citizen-developer scenarios.
Key Technologies: Microsoft Copilot Studio (primary low-code visual builder, Power Platform ALM), Agent 365 (Copilot Studio governance — Entra Agent ID, Purview, Defender), Azure Logic Apps (low-code MCP tools via APIM REST→MCP), Custom Control Plane UI (operational config), Azure API Center (skill registry), MAF .NET parity
POC Demo: POC1: Demonstrate Copilot Studio producing a deployed agent in <30 minutes (the 60-minute build benchmark from §6.4) — declarative artefacts Git-committed via Power Platform ALM, Entra Agent ID assigned via Agent 365. Also show a Logic App exposed as MCP tool, and a pro-code GHCP SDK + MAF workflow for the complex autonomous path.

Question: Can the platform agent construct new agents from natural language specifications? Describe the human-confirms, agent-builds-and-tests workflow.
Response: Yes — two modes. (1) Design-time agentic builder: a MAF agent executor generates new SKILL.md files and MAF workflow graph definitions from natural language. Workflow: (a) Human describes the desired capability (e.g. 'I need an agent that checks invoice amounts against historical averages and flags outliers'). (b) The agentic builder generates a SKILL.md with capability declaration, allowed tools, model selection, governance rules, plus a proposed MAF executor + validator pairing. (c) Submitted for human review via the Control Plane. (d) After approval, registered in Azure API Center at Design state. (e) Automated tests run (Foundry Evaluators). (f) Human confirms promotion to Preview, then Production (graph-topology changes go through APIOps PR review). (2) Runtime agent assembly (§6.2): MAF supports dynamic executor creation at runtime — a supervising agent executor can spawn a sub-workflow or persistent sub-agent within the domain's Hosted Agent scope. For persistent spawned agents, a governance-gate callback auto-registers the new agent in Entra Agent ID (new first-class agent identity) and Azure API Center (skill in Design state), and writes the spawning decision to the audit ledger. The spawned agent runs in Design state until a human operator promotes it to Production — enforcing the RFP requirement that 'persistent agents must be elevated into the same Data Plane storage schema as human-built agents, along the governance pathway'. No runtime escape from governance — all spawned agents follow the same API Center lifecycle as hand-written skills.
Key Technologies: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 (graph definitions as code, dynamic executor creation), GHCP SDK (agentic builder), SKILL.md generation, Azure API Center lifecycle (Design → Preview → Production), Entra Agent ID auto-registration, APIOps CI/CD, Foundry Evaluators
POC Demo: POC2: Demonstrate both — (1) design-time: describe a capability, agentic builder generates SKILL.md + MAF executor/validator pairing, human approves in API Center; (2) runtime assembly: Threadlight captures a new jurisdiction-specific compliance pattern mid-workflow, generates SKILL.md, auto-registers in Entra Agent ID + API Center Design state, human promotes to Production, new capability live in next workflow without redeploy.

Question: What pre-built agent templates, workflow patterns, and industry accelerators are available? Are templates forkable and customisable?
Response: Pre-built templates are available across both low-code (Copilot Studio) and pro-code (GHCP SDK + MAF) paths. The §6.4 RFP '60-minute build benchmark' is met natively by Copilot Studio: pick an agent template, add 3 pre-wired MCP tool connectors from the APIM-governed catalogue (each already configured with auth, rate limits, content safety), add 3 Foundry IQ knowledge sources, name the agent, publish to Agent 365. Target end-to-end build time: <30 minutes for a junior developer or seasoned UI user. Copilot Studio agents register in Entra Agent ID + Agent 365 automatically and are governed by APIM, Purview, and Defender. The Control Plane UI template forge provides a parallel path for consuming pre-wired pro-code templates (SKILL.md + MAF workflow snippets) when a deterministic graph is required; the APIOps pipeline handles registration in Entra Agent ID + API Center + APIM. Initial template library: (1) Talent Acquisition — skills for screening, sourcing, scheduling, compliance (US + DE variants), offer, onboarding. (2) Procure-to-Pay — skills for intake/OCR, three-way match, GL coding, routing, approval, payment, reconciliation. (3) Workflow orchestration patterns — DF envelope patterns plus MAF workflow graph templates (sequential, parallel fan-out, HITL gates, timer escalation, validator-chain compliance sub-graphs, Magentic-One multi-agent). Templates are forkable: fork creates a new Git branch, customise skills/connectors/knowledge for the specific agency/market/use case, deploy through the standard APIOps lifecycle. API Center tracks template lineage. Threadlight (Microsoft delivery accelerator) produces additional templates from SME interviews — output is SKILL.md + MAF workflow + MCP tool stubs, Git-inspectable, flows through the same governance pathway.
Key Technologies: Git template repositories, Azure API Center (template registry + lineage), Custom Control Plane UI template forge, APIOps CI/CD, Threadlight accelerator
POC Demo: POC1 close-out: observable 60-minute build demo — a junior developer builds, tests, and deploys a new agent (3 MCPs + 3 knowledge sources) via the Control Plane UI template forge in under 30 minutes. POC2: fork Talent Acquisition template for a specific WPP agency.
